speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har
text: asked the Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance whether the Government has data on (i) how Temasek Holdings’ total shareholder returns compare to other market benchmarks over the years (ii) how its portfolio of assets has shifted and is positioned for the future and (iii) how its portfolio of unlisted assets has performed and contributed to its overall performance to date.

speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar
text: asked the Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance in light of the drop in Temasek's 10-year Total Shareholder Returns to 6%, how does Temasek's long-term returns vary across the portfolio and how does each segment compare to benchmarks such as the MSCI World Index and Private Equity index.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: The data requested by Members are generally available on Temasek's website and annual reports.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: Broadly speaking, Temasek has outperformed these market indices over the long term.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: But it is important to recognise that Temasek is not a portfolio fund manager and the MSCI indices are not direct benchmarks for Temasek's performance.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: As a bottom-up investor, Temasek invests directly in companies.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: Temasek started with the Singapore companies it owned and subsequently expanded to take stakes in companies in Asia.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: Temasek has only recently invested more actively in North America and Europe.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: Therefore, its portfolio for now is still Asia-centric, with about two-thirds exposure in Asia.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: On the other hand, the composition of indices varies significantly from Temasek's portfolio.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: For instance, MSCI World Index and ACWI have larger weightages to the US stock market, which has done very well over the last 10 years compared to Asian stock markets.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: This is why there will be occasions when Temasek's returns are higher than the MSCI World Index and ACWI, and other occasions when the returns are not as high as these indices.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: On comparisons with other sovereign wealth funds, we have previously explained that it is not straightforward to make such comparisons because the funds have different mandates, investment approaches and risk profiles.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: There are also funds, like Saudi Arabia's Public Investment Fund, that do not report their performance on the same basis as Temasek.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: To position its portfolio for the future, Temasek has stated that it is focused on building a resilient portfolio that can withstand exogenous shocks while capturing growth opportunities.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: As shareholder, the Government's role is to ensure that Temasek has a competent board to oversee its management and ensure that its mandate is met.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: The Government will continue to hold Temasek accountable for delivering good long-term returns on the overall investment portfolio.

speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
text: I have two supplementary questions for the Senior Minister of State.

speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
text: The first one is about Temasek's unlisted assets, comprising 53% of the portfolio as at 31 March 2023.

speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
text: Temasek had shared – and I think, the Senior Minister of State has also touched on that – if the unlisted portfolio was marked to market, it would provide $18 billion of value uplift.

speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
text: So, my question is, given the dominance of unlisted assets in its portfolio, what are the plans for Temasek to reflect the underlying value of this portfolio in reporting shareholder returns going forward; and also, the impact of this unlisted assets' performance in its contributions to its Net Investment Returns Contribution (NIRC) for Singapore's Budget?

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: Ms Foo also asked about the impact on NIRC.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: What this means is that the annual fluctuations to our entities' returns do not directly impact the NIRC at all.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: I have two supplementary questions for Senior Minister of State Chee.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: The first is with regards to the losses mentioned in my Parliamentary Question.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: I mentioned that the net value of the portfolio shrunk by $21 billion.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: I think the Senior Minister of State mentioned it somewhat just now, but can he reassure the House that Temasek's losses or gains in terms of threshold of returns historically, will there be ways where the Senior Minister of State can highlight that, given the worst-case scenario going forward, what thresholds should we be comfortable with in term of dollars in million or billion amounts every year?

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: The second question I have is, the Senior Minister of State mentioned just now that the focus on Asia is about two-thirds, if I am not mistaken.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: Can the Senior Minister of State share, given the investment climate, Temasek's assessment or the Ministry of Finance's (MOF) assessment going forward?

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: To what extent will be Temasek's investment domestically versus overseas going forward, given circumstances if things require domestic investments, that is, investments needed in Singapore?

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: As I mentioned in my reply, what the Government will do is to look at the overall portfolio returns for Temasek over the longer term.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: I think the board will set certain benchmarks to measure the performance of management.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: As the Government, we will certainly hold Temasek accountable for the overall long-term returns.

speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
text: Can I just clarify if the unlisted investments here would be comparable to private equity investments, which I think have had long-term returns north of 12% to 15%?

speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
text: So, if you are saying 10% for Temasek, is this the right comparison?

speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
text: My second supplementary question is, could you also share the returns by geography, in particular, Singapore, China and then something that is more comparable to the MSCI?

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: They include private equity, but they also include infrastructure and real estate.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: The comparisons are not one-to-one with some of the other fund managers that Ms Mariam may be referring to.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: I do not have the data in front of me right now, but as I had also explained, Temasek is not a portfolio fund manager.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
text: Speaker, can I ask the Senior Minister of State again?

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
text: Sorry, I did not get that explanation in Temasek's report.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: The numbers that he referred to, the numbers that he wanted to clarify, I believe these are already explained by Temasek in their annual report.
